text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT

- The president should not be turned into a figurehead, says Finance Minister Sauli Niinisto, rejecting a proposal from parliament's constitutional committee to divide foreign policy powers between the president and the government.
- The value of Finnish mutual funds has risen above 15 billion markka this year, and customised portfolio management services are also a growth business.
- Expanded out-patient care for eldery people has increased injuries and deaths in domestic fires, safety officials say.
- Warm weather has produced big rafts of blue-green algae in the Gulf of Finland -- the biggest in ten years, frontier guard pilots say.
- R&D unit of Finnish telecoms group Nokia is offering internships for gifted young mathematicians who begin concentrating on computer science already in high school.
- A bear knocked down a jogger on a forest road in eastern Finland, clawed him and bit him on the jaw, then left him alone with only minor injuries.
KAUPPALEHTI
- Finnish food group Raisio plans to launch its colesterol-lowering margarine Benecol in Sweden this autumn.
- In future state-owned Postipankki will not settle for being only a local bank -- an alliance with a foreign bank is an option, says the chairman of the bank's supervisory board.
- At end-June, foreign investors owned more than half of Finnish media group Aamulehti and over 40 percent of publishing group Talentum.
- Paper machine maker Valmet says its doctorate programme has spawned innovations and patent applications.
AAMULEHTI
- Sudden wealth can endanger a lottery winner's mental health, and the state lottery should consider limiting the size of its biggest payouts, Finnish mental society says.
- The Finnish Red Cross has developed a suitcase-sized operating room that can be assembled in 20 minutes.
TURUN SANOMAT
- Finland and France have the lowest inflation levels in the European Union: Finland's May inflation 0.9 percent.
- Lithuanians have taken the lead in suicide statistics over the Finns, Lithuanian expert says.
- Green Party leader Satu Hassi's proposal to nominate environment minister Pekka Haavisto as the Greens' presidential candidate divides party members.
DEMARI
- Helsinki telephone company HPY has launched a new low-priced mobile phone stardard, DCS, in the capital city region.
-- Nora Hallberg, Helsinki Newsroom +358-9-680 50 292
